To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of NYP, omentin, and visfatin is comparable between obese patients and controls, whereas visfatin is lower in obese individuals.
in obese adults plasma NPY levels are comparable to non-obese controls, and the expression of NYP, omentin, visfatin is comparable between obese individuals, and controls.

in our obese adults, glucocorticoid levels were lower, plasma NPY concentrations were comparable between obese individuals compared with healthy controls, and the expression of NYP, omentin, and visfatin, as well as cortisol, was comparable between obese and control subjects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of neopeptide Y, omentin, and visfatin and their association with clinical parameters in adipose tissue.
the regulation of NPY and adipose tissue-derived hormones in obesity.
the role of adipose tissue in the pathophysiology of obesity and its complications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NPY is detectable in adipocytes, but its expression does not differ between obese and non-obese adults.
the expression of NYP, omentin, and visfatin are not related to endocrine or clinical parameters in our obese adults.
the expression of the investigated adipose tissue derived peptides in the adipose tissues is not altered in obese adults compared to controls.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NPY is detectable in adipocytes, omentin is predominantly expressed in visceral adipose tissue, and visfatin is lower in subcutaneous fat of obese patients.
the expression of NYP, omentin, and visfatin is comparable between obese and controls, and is not related to plasma cortisol concentrations.
the expression of adipokines and the endocrine milieu in obesity are not as straightforward as expected.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of NYP and omentin is not altered in obese patients, while the expression of visfatin is decreased.
the expression of adipose tissue NPY, omental and visfatin is comparable between obese and lean subjects, while the expression of visfatin in the subcutaneus fat is lower in obese individuals.
the expression of NYP, omentin, and visfatin is not elevated in obese adults, and that the glucocorticoids were not increased in our patients.
